lines.trans: Relax. Nobody will come in here—this space belongs just to the two of us.
Okay.
First, we strip away everything dressing you up.
Common sense and rules—cast away everything that ties you down.
Your unadorned face is much lovelier.
From the very beginning, I had decided to have you film my first work, Mr. Muranishi.
What would you have done if it hadn't turned out that way?
I intended to have you film me no matter what means it took.
That's a great look on your face.
Your expression still looks a bit stiff.
Let the tension out of your shoulders.
Now then, this is the moment to take that first step forward.

examples.text: リラックスして。ここには誰も入ってこない、二人だけの空間。
examples.trans: Relax. Nobody will come in here—this space belongs just to the two of us.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Godan verb: potential polite 入れます (はいれます) means 'can enter'.

examples.text: 予約なしでも入れますか。
examples.trans: Can we get in without a reservation?

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Noun.

examples.text: 今日は空がとても青いですね。
examples.trans: The sky is very blue today, isn't it?
Birds are flying in the sky.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: まずは君を飾ってるすべてを剥ぎ取る。
examples.trans: First, we strip away everything dressing you up.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used adverbially or as a noun to mean 'everything' or 'all of them'.

examples.text: すべてうまくいきました。
まずは君を飾ってるすべてを剥ぎ取る。
examples.trans: First, we strip away everything dressing you up.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: to tie; to bind; to restrict
meanings.note: Often used figuratively in the passive 縛られる ('to be bound by').

examples.text: ルールに縛られたくない。
examples.trans: I don't want to be bound by rules.
Tie up the luggage with string.

examples.text: 常識もルールも、君を縛るすべてを捨て去るんだ。
examples.trans: Common sense and rules—cast away everything that ties you down.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

examples.text: 素顔のほうがステキだ。
examples.trans: Your unadorned face is much lovelier.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: おはようございます。皆さんステキですわ。
examples.trans: Good morning. You all look wonderful.

examples.text: ホントにステキなセンスですね。どうしてお仕事お辞めになられたんですか？
examples.trans: You truly have lovely taste. Why did you leave your job?

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: お話聞いておりました。一作目にはわたくしも参加できますの？
examples.trans: I heard about your plan. May I also take part in the first film?

examples.text: 一作目はインパクトが何よりも大事だ。質よりもインパクトだ。
examples.trans: For the first film, impact matters more than anything. Impact over quality.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Ichidan verb; potential form 決められる means 'can decide'.

examples.text: まだ何も決めていません。
今決められないなら、後で考えましょう。
examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.en: what kind of; what sort of
meanings.note: Interrogative prenominal modifier.

examples.text: どんな音楽を聴きますか。
examples.trans: What kind of music do you listen to?

examples.text: どんな仕事をしているんですか。
examples.trans: What kind of work do you do?

meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.trans: Let the tension out of your shoulders.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Prompts someone into action or shoos them along.

examples.text: でも最初の一歩を踏み出すのは難しいですよね。私もそうでした。
examples.trans: Still, taking that very first step is hard, isn't it? It was the same for me.

examples.text: 誰にでも一歩踏み出すべき時には、今だってお知らせが来るの。
examples.trans: For everyone, when it's truly time to take a step forward, a notice arrives saying now is the moment.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: その瞬間を待っていた。
examples.trans: I was waiting for that moment.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
